items.title: Transformers can be over 99 percent efficient — better than almost any machine
items.claim: A large power-station step-up transformer is around 99.5 percent efficient. A typical car engine is about 25 percent. Most domestic appliances are 30-80 percent. Transformers convert AC voltage with almost no loss.
items.prompt: How is a passive iron-and-copper device so efficient?

options.text: It contains no moving parts to wear out

Transformers have no thermodynamic Carnot limit because they don't go via heat — they exchange energy magnetically by mutual induction; losses are limited to ohmic heating in windings, eddy currents and core hysteresis
They store energy and return it later

items.reveal:
A transformer has two coils wound around a shared iron core. AC in the primary creates an oscillating magnetic flux through the core; the flux induces an EMF in the secondary equal to V_secondary = (N_secondary / N_primary) × V_primary.

Losses come from: (1) ohmic heating in the windings (I squared R), (2) eddy currents induced in the iron core (suppressed by laminating the core into thin insulated sheets), (3) hysteresis losses as the iron magnetises and demagnetises 100 times per second (50 Hz, both polarities).

A well-designed transformer at full load loses about 0.5 percent. Empty (no load on secondary), losses fall to a fraction of a percent. The same physics underlies wireless phone chargers — inductive coupling at higher frequencies.
items.why: Transformers look passive and boring. They are among the most efficient energy-conversion devices humans have ever built.

items.title: A vacuum flask works by blocking three different things at once
items.claim: A Thermos flask keeps coffee hot for hours by simultaneously blocking conduction (vacuum gap), convection (no air to circulate), and radiation (silvered inner walls). Each mechanism alone wouldn't be enough.

options.text: The three heat-transfer mechanisms operate by different physical processes; blocking only one allows the others to dominate. The vacuum eliminates conduction and convection through air; the silvered walls reflect infrared radiation back into the contents
Conduction is the slowest by itself
Each layer cools a different temperature range

items.reveal:
Conduction: kinetic energy transferred between atoms in contact. Best blocked by removing matter (vacuum) or using poor thermal conductors (foam, fibreglass).

Convection: bulk movement of fluid carrying heat. Best blocked by removing the fluid or preventing flow (sealed cells, vacuum).

Radiation: infrared electromagnetic waves emitted by warm surfaces. Best blocked by reflective (low-emissivity) surfaces or by interposing reflective layers.

A vacuum flask combines all three: the vacuum gap suppresses conduction and convection between inner and outer walls; the silvered inner surface reflects infrared back to the contents instead of letting it radiate out. Modern double-walled stainless steel travel mugs do the same.

Space blankets exploit the radiation channel — a thin metallised film reflects up to 97 percent of body radiation back at the wearer.
items.why: Heat transfer is taught as three separate topics. Real insulation problems require considering all three at once — and a vacuum flask is the classic case.

items.title: Reading a meniscus from the wrong angle changes the answer
items.claim: Read a burette with your eye above the meniscus: you see a high reading. Read with your eye below: a low reading. The error can be several percent — purely from where you put your head.
items.prompt: What's the right way to take the reading?

options.text: Eye level with the meniscus, viewing perpendicular to the scale, so the line of sight passes through the bottom of the meniscus and the scale at the same level
From slightly above to see the bottom of the meniscus better
From below to avoid disturbing the liquid

items.reveal:
Parallax error happens when the object you are reading and the scale you are reading against are at different distances from your eye. Any tilt in viewing angle shifts the apparent position of one relative to the other.

For a meniscus in a burette: the liquid surface and the scale on the burette tube are separated by a few millimetres. Looking down or up at an angle moves them apparently relative to each other.

Same problem with ammeters and voltmeters with mirror scales: align your eye so the needle and its reflection in the mirror coincide. This way you know you're looking perpendicular.

Digital readouts eliminate parallax (the reading is a single number). They introduce other concerns: rounding, response time, calibration drift.
items.why: Lab errors are taught as 'be careful'. Parallax is a specific systematic error with a specific fix — eye level, perpendicular sighting.
